newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes ride wave higher on heating oil rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes ride wave higher on heating oil rally.

text.p: Huge gains in the heating oil futures complex pumped life into the outright U.S. cash crude price Friday, ending the week strong on fears cold weather forecasts would impact precariously tight inventories.
January West Texas Intermediate/Cushing closed out 75 cents higher at $24.40-50 a barrel.
Cash grade trading failed to excite, though, finding only nominal interest in adjusting differentials heading into the weekend, traders said.
Some forecasts called for a blast of Artic air throughout the United States next week, testing distillate supply levels.
NYMEX options expiration for December contracts also played into the extreme strength in spot crude, traders said.
A lack of volume in the cash grade trade was blamed on an industry function in New Orleans, Louisiana, which drew traders both on Thursday and Friday.
"It was difficult to find bodies today," said one trader.
Grades that were traded included Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at a 69-70 cts premium to the Jan WTI/Cushing, right in line with closing levels Thursday.
WTI/Midland was sold early at 2-3 cts below the Jan WTI, before recovering to the unchanged level.
Jan Postings Plus at Cushing was done at slightly firmer marks at $2.24-$2.26, traders said.
Aftermarket dealings also saw a WTI outright trade at $22.42 a barrel.
